function: ISAC constellation design: two MLPs generate the constellation points, trained on a unified KLD loss that balances BER and target detection; beamforming uses SDR, not learning (p. 3).
system: ISAC BS with M antennas, one single-antenna user, extended target; learned constellation design posed for single-antenna set-up; no RIS; frequency band not stated (p. 1, 3).
method: Two MLPs (five fully connected layers, ReLU) generate real and imaginary parts of constellation points with tanh amplitude remap; trained by backpropagation on the unified KLD loss (p. 3-4).
data_channel: No training data described; Monte-Carlo simulation with Saleh-Valenzuela communication channel (LoS plus P=4 NLoS paths) and extended target with J=10 scatterers (p. 1, 4).
test_conditions: Constellations designed for Q=16 and Q=32 and several weighting factors; Pareto bounds for sensing-communication angle 10 and 90 degrees; no test in unseen conditions (p. 4-5).
baselines: Commonly used constellations (PSK, APSK) only, non-learned; no earlier learned design or other optimization method compared (p. 5).
metrics: KLD for communication and radar, bit error rate, probability of successful detection (2D-CFAR, PFA=1e-5), minimum constellation distance (p. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 1: "the Saleh-Valenzuela channel model, consisting of both one line-of-sight (LoS) and several non-LoS (NLoS) paths"
q2_support: p. 4: "Two modulation orders are considered, i.e., Q = 16 and Q = 32"
q3_support: p. 5: "we also illustrate the sensing and communication capabilities of other commonly used constellations"
q4_support: p. 3: "with each composed of five cascaded fully connected layers and using ReLU as the activation function"
q5_support: p. 4: "The BS-user distance and BS-target distance are set as dc = 800 m and dt = 1000 m"
notes: PDF is arXiv:2405.10553v1 (5 pages), Revealing the Trade-off in ISAC Systems: The KL Divergence Perspective; it prints no DOI. Borderline eligibility, included as area 5. The only learned part is the MLP constellation design, posed for the single-antenna set-up (p. 3, Sec. III) with a loss that depends only on the constellation points (Eq. 15); the M-antenna beamforming is solved by SDR, not learned (p. 4). Included because the BS has M antennas (p. 1) and the learned design serves sensing and communication, but the reviewer may prefer exclusion under system or no_learning. q1 not met: own Monte-Carlo simulator with the textbook Saleh-Valenzuela model (p. 4). q2 not met: no trained model is tested in a new scenario. q3 not met: only PSK and APSK constellations (Fig. 5), no earlier learned design. q4 not met: architecture is described but no operations, parameters or runtime. q5 not met: no code or data link, no public dataset; M is never given.
